sanjay: Pushing a small canary of CUDA Toolkit 12.1.3 images to eu-west GPU nodes. Noticed several nodes flapping health checks and container restarts during the push. Cordoning affected hosts and rolling back the tag for now.

infra-automate: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: redwood/toolkit:12.1.3 -> 12.1.4-canary (digest updated). Automated probes flagged 7 nodes failing GPU health and NCCL handshakes at 2026-03-18T09:02:12Z.

olivia: Can someone paste the failing pod logs and node metadata? suspect host driver vs container runtime mismatch or missing ABI symbols.

dmitri: Here's a representative container log from a restarted worker pod:
```
[2026-03-18T09:02:13Z] runtime: cudaGetDeviceCount returned 0
[2026-03-18T09:02:13Z] WARN NCCL: init rank 0 failed: internal error
[2026-03-18T09:02:15Z] NET/Socket: recv failed: Connection timed out
[2026-03-18T09:02:16Z] error: /usr/local/lib/libnccl.so.2: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not found (required by /app/bin/worker)
```
Node info: driver=530.41.22, kernel=5.15.0-100-generic, glibc=2.31. Image toolchain: built on ubuntu22 with gcc-13 (libstdc++ from gcc-13).

lucy: That exact "GLIBCXX_3.4.30 not found" is an ABI mismatch between container libs and host-provided libstdc++ when native libs are dlopen'd (NCCL or plugin .so). Also sees some socket timeouts that could be RDMA/ib verbs negotiation failing with new toolkit changes.

oncall-maya: Stopping new pod admissions to eu-west GPU pool, moving probe traffic to us-central, and pausing cluster-autoscaler for eu-west to avoid noisy spin-ups.

olivia: Confirmed: 4 canary tasks reprovisioned to us-central and are stable. No Dedicated pools were updated so they are fine. Shared on-demand instances in eu-west had restart churn. Finance: quick cost hit if this continues (cross-region moves + extra spinups).

finance: Noted. Rough cost exposure if left ~ $3.8k/day for the extra egress and spinups. Escalating to leadership.

dmitri: Quick mitigation options we tested locally: 
- rebuild the image pinning to gcc-11 (ENV CC=gcc-11 CXX=g++-11) so libstdc++ matches older host ABI
- bundle a compatible libstdc++.so.6 inside the image under /opt/compat/lib but ensure rpath/ldconfig picks it up (safer than bind-mounting host libs)
- temporary perf workaround: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 and NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 to disable RDMA, this avoids some net-level failures at ~15% perf cost
- run `ldd /app/bin/worker` and `strings /usr/local/lib/libnccl.so.2 | grep GLIBCXX` inside canary container as a smoke test

lucy: Long-term: add a build matrix in CI to produce images built with gcc-11 and gcc-13, and run them through a kernel-driver matrix matching our node fleet (kernels: 5.10, 5.15, 6.1; drivers: 525.x, 530.x). Also add an explicit "libstdc++ ABI tag" label in image manifests and gate canaries on that.

sanjay: Rollback action: reverted canary tag to redwood/toolkit:11.8.9-stable on the affected eu-west nodes, drained and restarted workloads. Monitoring sliding window 30m. If stable, re-run a small canary with gcc-11 pinned images.

infra-automate: incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0318-02 (cuda12-abi-toolchain-surge). Severity: P2. Teams: eng-infra, eng-runtime. Runbook link: /runbooks/cuda-toolkit-upgrades.md

oncall-maya: Ops checklist executed: cordon/taint affected nodes, annotate `cu-toolkit-canary-failed=true`, disable autoscaler for region until manual rollback completes.

olivia: Added short-term runbook note: for toolkit rollouts, run `docker run --rm <image> bash -lc "strings /usr/local/lib/libnccl.so.2 | grep GLIBCXX || true"` as a preflight. Also add `cudaGetDeviceCount` sanity check to canary health probes.

dmitri: Documented an internal workaround in the playbook: if ABI errors seen, prefer rebuild-with-gcc11 path over bind-mounting host libs. Bind-mount is a last-resort and annotated as high-risk.

lucy: :thumbsup: Keep posting any new undefined symbol strings or kernel oops. We'll prefer small, instrumented canaries after CI adds the ABI checks.

sanjay: Status update 09:45Z: 30m post-rollback looks stable in eu-west. Closing immediate blast window. Will schedule a follow-up retro + CI gating ticket.
